extracted.intended_audience: IB Diploma students (and teachers/tutors) preparing Internal Assessments in Math, English, Chemistry and Biology
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the IB Internal Assessment (IA) marking rubrics for popular Diploma Programme subjects (Math, English, Chemistry, Biology), explaining the assessment criteria and guidance for scoring high marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (/4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the organisation and coherence of your exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure it in a way that is logically developed and easy to follow: Introduction, Body, Conclusion. Use relevant graphs, tables, and diagrams to accompany the work. Avoid unnecessary or repetitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Communication (/4)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurate and consistent mathematical terminology, symbols and notation. Explain key terms, variables and concepts. All calculations are explained and the data used is described. Represent your math in various forms — including formulas, graphs, tables, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Engagement (/3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes thinking independently and creatively; connects the exploration to the student's personal interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect the IA's exploration subject to your own personal interest. Explore the topic from various viewpoints. Show independent/creative thinking. Include expansions to the study and demonstrate personal initiative in topic choice and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection (/3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Involves reviewing, analysing and evaluating your exploration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a final evaluation that links back to the initial objective of the report. Analyse both strengths and weaknesses of the exploration. Include suggestions for improvements. Ensure evaluation is relevant and shows critical review of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Mathematics (/6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Involves the use of mathematics appropriate to the student's level (SL or HL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use relevant mathematics based on your level; avoid unnecessary math. Any math beyond the syllabus must be clarified and explained. Formulate predictions and conduct tests where appropriate. The mathematics explored must be correct and all calculations must have explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge, understanding and interpretation (/10) — English IA
rubrics_metrics.description: Grades how well the student shows knowledge and understanding of the extracts, and the literary work and non-literary body of work from which they were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show perceptive knowledge and understanding of the text. Ensure interpretations are consistently relevant to your chosen global issue. Support points with convincing references to extracts and the body of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis and Evaluation (/10) — English IA
rubrics_metrics.description: Marks the extent to which your oral analyses and evaluates how the author presents the global issue through authorial choices in the extracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show insightful analysis and evaluation of how authors present global issues through authorial choices. Effectively support analysis with references to specific authorial techniques and their effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence, balance, focus and organisation (/10) — English IA
rubrics_metrics.description: Centred around how coherent, balanced and focused your oral is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show effective coherence, balance, and focus — for example, spending an equal amount of time analysing each text and focusing on the authorial choices that present your global issue. Maintain a clear, logical organisation throughout the oral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language (/10) — English IA
rubrics_metrics.description: Grades vocabulary, jargon, and overall effectiveness of language use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be accurate and varied in your vocabulary, style, syntax and terminology. Use language that clearly conveys your analysis and interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Design (/6) — Chemistry & Biology IA
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses how well-structured your investigation process is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a clearly defined research question. Discuss background theory relevant to your research question. Explain the methodology thoroughly — apparatus used, the procedure and why, and measurement units. Communicate how the data was recorded and processed. Address safety, ethical, and environmental issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis and Evaluation (/6) — Chemistry & Biology IA
rubrics_metrics.description: Grades how you process and interpret the data to formulate a conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly communicate how the data was recorded and processed. Interpret uncertainties and outliers. Use accepted literature values and compare them to your results. Ensure graphs, tables and figures are labelled, annotated, use correct units and standard decimal places. Avoid major inaccuracies or inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion (/6) — Chemistry & Biology IA
rubrics_metrics.description: Revolves around your final conclusion and its relation to the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a conclusion that is relevant to the research question and consistent with the data analysis. Ensure your conclusion is supported and justified by the analysis you conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (/6) — Chemistry & Biology IA
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the evaluation section assessing reflection on methodology and investigation quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss methodological weaknesses or limitations and possible solutions. Explain the relative impacts of methodological weaknesses on the data and uncertainties. Identify realistic improvements related to the identified weaknesses and limitations. Discuss a proposed extension to further investigate your topic.
